explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM and human judgments on the same dataset using correlation analysis and agreement metrics

prompts.notes: Paper mentions using 3 prompts but only reports best-performing prompt in main text; full prompts are in Appendix B

guidelines.notes: Human annotators rated reading ease on 1-5 scale (1=very poor, 5=very high); uses existing dataset from prior work

sample_size.notes: Uses dataset of 60 summaries from prior work, all evaluated by both LLM and human judges

quantitative_scores.notes: Best performing model correlation with human judgments

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Traditional metrics with <0.3 Pearson correlation considered 'poor'

validation_results.summary_finding: LLMs outperform traditional readability metrics, with best model achieving 0.56 Pearson correlation with human judgments, indicating better alignment than traditional metrics which averaged <0.3 correlation.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluate reading ease on same 1-5 scale; LLMs additionally provide reasoning about deeper readability attributes
